title: SprintBridge SDK bootstrapping, auth & faststart lab
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood SDK quickstart (Python + TypeScript), authentication patterns for VPC/private deployment, and faststart lab to get a sandbox up for a short pilot. Covered hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs plus Optimize hints for batching and caching.
topics: Auth: API key vs SSO/SAML vs VPC private control plane
Next steps: bench run and pilot checklist
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: ok hi everyone, thanks for hopping on, i'm maya from Redwood Inference / AE, we also have lucas who's our se, and jordan in the background, super quick agenda
00:14 Riya Patel: hey thanks, i'm riya, lead ml eng at sprintbridge, we are the team building the search & summarization feature, excited to see the quickstart
00:25 Lucas Park: today we'll do a two-part flow: first get you a working python and typescript quickstart running in your sandbox, then cover auth patterns and some optimize tips, and leave time for questions
00:39 Evan Tran: timeline wise we'd like a pilot by end of nov, low-latency under 120ms p50 is ideal, and of course data never leaves our vpc
00:53 Carlos Mendes: also need SOC2/ISO compliance checklist and how KMS integrates, we manage keys in aws-kms
01:05 Lucas Park: great notes, we'll show the private control plane flow and how to wire in your kms; one note, some transcriptions may swap names — "redwood console" shows as redwood console or redwood control plane in the docs
01:18 Maya Chen: jumping into the quickstart: pip install redwood-sdk, npm i @redwood/inference-sdk (voiceover: sometimes package names get transcribed wrong, actual repo link will be shared)
01:33 Riya Patel: quick q, do we need a dedicated pool to start or can we use hosted?
01:38 Lucas Park: you can start on hosted api to validate latencies and correctness, then move to dedicated for predictable throughput; for strict data residency and no egress from your vpc, use private deployment
01:52 Carlos Mendes: and for private, how's network — do we run an agent that tunnels or do you ship a package?
01:58 Lucas Park: we have a private control plane option that orchestrates an on-prem runtime you host; for cloud VPCs we support a customer-managed VPC peering or private link style connection, and yes there's an on-prem package if you need air-gapped
02:12 Evan Tran: okay good. can we see the code snippet for authenticating with an api key and then with sso?
02:18 Maya Chen: sure — python example: from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) then client.chat.create(...). For sso we map SAML SSO to orgs and provision short-lived tokens issued by your IdP
02:35 Riya Patel: do the tokens support RBAC role scoping?
02:39 Lucas Park: yes, tokens can be scoped to routes and models via role policies. We'll show a sample policy in the security docs we send
02:50 Maya Chen: for the typescript quickstart: import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference-sdk'; const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
03:04 Riya Patel: any caveats with nextjs serverless lambdas acquiring tokens? we have warm containers and cold starts
03:12 Lucas Park: main gotcha is ephemeral environments — keep your tokens in your secrets manager (github actions / aws secrets manager) and use short-lived tokens for workloads that run on client side — also server-side you can persist the api key in a secret store
03:26 Carlos Mendes: about ci/cd, how do we provision sandbox keys for infra folks without giving full prod access?
03:31 Maya Chen: create org-level sandbox with role-limited service accounts; we'll send a script that creates sandbox org, service account, and scoped API key
03:44 Lucas Park: quick demo switch to the console — showing tokens page, org roles, and per-route quotas (note: minor audio cut)
03:55 Riya Patel: transcript says "per route quotas" as something else earlier, but we saw it on the console
04:02 Maya Chen: moving on to Optimize, we recommend three levers: batching, prefix/kv caching, and quantization profile selection based on latency vs quality
04:13 Lucas Park: for your workload (search + summarize) prefix caching helps a lot if you reuse system prompts; batching helps for throughput but increases p95 if you need strict latency
04:27 Riya Patel: curious about quantization, we are on A100s in prod for embeddings — can we get recommendations?
04:33 Lucas Park: yes, we'll run a quick profile; our optimize tool suggests q4_0 or q5_1 for encoder chi? (several words mid transcribed) we'll attach a profile report after a small sample
04:49 Maya Chen: i'll note that for the bench — speaking of bench, would you want us to run a latency+cost benchmark using a sample of your traffic?
04:56 Evan Tran: yes, that would be useful, include p50/p95, token cost estimates, and a compare between hosted/dedicated/private
05:06 Maya Chen: noted. we'll need a small sample prompt set and expected qps distribution
05:12 Riya Patel: i'll compile that, probably 1k sample chats + 1000 embedding requests, average seq length around 512 tokens
05:20 Carlos Mendes: security questions: SOC2, iso, audit logs retention, and KMS integration
05:26 Maya Chen: we are SOC2 compliant, and have enterprise SKUs for longer retention; KMS integration is available for private and dedicated — you'll manage the CMKs, we call out usage in audit logs
05:38 Lucas Park: also note S3 access patterns if you plan to use object store for large vector shards — we'll share the recommended IAM policy
05:48 Riya Patel: what about telemetry and observability into token-level cost?
05:53 Lucas Park: console exposes token breakdown per route, and you can stream traces to your datadog or honeycomb via our tracing hooks
06:02 Maya Chen: small tangent — we sometimes see "kv cache" transcribed as "kay vee" but it's the same idea: cache past key/value attention to speed up subsequent tokens
06:14 Evan Tran: any limitations on model versions for private?
06:18 Lucas Park: you can pin model versions; some bleeding-edge opt kernels may be restricted on certain hardware — we'll list compatibility matrix in the onboarding doc we send
06:30 Riya Patel: let's run the quickstart now, we have two devs who can pair
06:35 Lucas Park: ok i'll paste the python quickstart gist in chat: - git clone github.com/redwood/inference-quickstarts (link will be sent), - cd python-quickstart, - pip install -r requirements.txt, - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=... , - python run_chat.py
06:54 (typing sounds)
07:00 Riya Patel: running now... getting "403 unauthorized"
07:04 Maya Chen: that usually means the key isn't scoped to the org or missing org id header; for hosted we accept api_key alone, but for private you need to include X-Org-Id header or set REDWOOD_ORG in env
07:18 Carlos Mendes: hmm we used the sandbox key from the email, maybe it was scoped to a different org
07:23 Maya Chen: i'll reissue a scoped sandbox key after the call, but let's also confirm your env vars: run env | grep REDWOOD
07:38 Riya Patel: ok confirmed REDWOOD_API_KEY is set, no REDWOOD_ORG
07:43 Maya Chen: that explains it — set REDWOOD_ORG=sprintbridge-sandbox and rerun
07:51 Riya Patel: rerunning... now chat returns tokens, yay, we see partial garbling in transcript sometimes but responses look good
08:05 Evan Tran: latency on this quickstart from our laptop is around 150ms p50, what's reasonable to expect in hosted?
08:14 Lucas Park: quickstart often hits public internet network variances; our hosted p50 for similar configs is ~80-120ms depending on model; in dedicated you'll get more consistent p50 and better p95
08:27 Riya Patel: any client-side batching patterns I'd need to change?
08:31 Lucas Park: if you use streaming responses, keep chunk size smaller; for non-streaming, group small requests up to a batching window (e.g., 20-50ms) to improve throughput but test p95 impact
08:44 Carlos Mendes: for embeddings, can we do bulk upsert to your vectors api with retries?
08:49 Lucas Park: yes, the SDK has a batch embeddings helper with idempotent retry keys; we'll include a sample in the repo
08:58 Maya Chen: quick pause for questions
09:02 Riya Patel: what's the quickest path to start a 30-day pilot on dedicated GPUs?
09:07 Maya Chen: we can provision a small dedicated pool for a trial; it'll be on a reserved commit but we can do a short-term eval billing arrangement — i'll escalate with ops once you sign an MOU
09:21 Evan Tran: price ballpark?
09:24 Maya Chen: i'll include a pilot pricing sheet in the follow-up, with token-based and fixed pool options
09:32 Carlos Mendes: any recommended observability hooks we should add now?
09:36 Lucas Park: instrument per-route telemetry, add tracing hooks near request creation and include the token_cost header, and export to your existing APM
09:49 Riya Patel: great, thanks — let's recap next steps
09:53 Maya Chen: recap: we'll send quickstart repo, sandbox key(s), security docs (SOC2, KMS integration), bench questionnaire, and a pilot pricing sheet
10:10 Evan Tran: schedule a follow-up bench review next week
10:14 Maya Chen: i'll send a Doodle, thanks everyone
10:20 (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "q4_0" typed as "qfor zero" in one spot). Links and repo references will be provided in the follow-up email. There was minor crosstalk during the console demo when the audio hit a packet loss moment.
